findings.title: _source decryption uses the raw ES `_id` and the wrong namespace, so the AAD never matches.
findings.body: `rawId` is the Elasticsearch document `_id` from `METADATA _id`. In the saved objects index that id carries a prefix (`<type>:<id>`, and `<namespace>:<type>:<id>` for single-namespace types). It is not the saved object id. Also, single-namespace documents store `namespace` rather than `namespaces`, so `source.namespaces` is undefined and the descriptor namespace is lost. Both the id and the namespace go into the AAD. As a result, `decryptOrStripResponseAttributes` hits an AAD mismatch on every row: each row's encrypted attributes are stripped instead of decrypted, and a decryption error is logged per row. The documented decrypt path never works, and the unit test only passes because it mocks the extension. Fix: convert the raw document first, using the serializer (`rawToSavedObject`) or the same helpers that `find`/`search` use, so the real id and namespaces are recovered before decrypting.

findings.title: Requesting `_source` without `_id` returns encrypted attributes untouched.
findings.body: With `metadata: ['_source']` (no `_id`), `decryptSourceColumn` returns early. `stripEncryptedColumns` only checks `<type>.<attr>` columns, so the `_source` objects reach the caller with the raw encrypted attribute values inside. The integration with `find`/`search` never exposes those values this way. Fix: when `_source` is present but decryption can't run, remove the encrypted attributes from `_source` (use `getEncryptedAttributes` to find them), or require `_id` whenever `_source` is requested.

findings.title: Encrypted column masking only matches exact column names, so renaming gets past it.
findings.body: Columns are nulled only when the name is exactly `<type>.<attr>`. A pipeline like `| EVAL s = connector.secrets` or `| RENAME connector.secrets AS s` returns the encrypted value under a different name, and it passes through unmasked. The tutorial and JSDoc promise that encrypted scalar columns are "always" nulled, which does not hold. Fix: reject pipelines that reference encrypted attribute fields, or trace columns back to their source fields with the ES|QL parser, rather than matching output names.

findings.title: The agent's working files (`tasks/prd.json`, `tasks/progress.txt`) are committed to the repo.
findings.body: These are scratch files from the agent's own loop: a PRD with `passes` flags and a progress log with local notes. They are not part of the feature, and nothing in the request asks for them. Merging them adds a top-level `tasks/` directory to the Kibana repo. Remove both files from the PR.

findings.title: The pipeline check doesn't stop changes to the generated `FROM` clause or lookups against other indices.
findings.body: The only check is a regex for a leading `FROM|ROW|SHOW|METRICS`. The pipeline is then joined with a plain `${fromClause} ${pipeline}`. A pipeline such as `, other-index METADATA _source | ...` therefore adds more indices to the `FROM` that runs with kibana_system privileges, which goes against the claim that index resolution is controlled by `type`. Commands later in the pipeline (`LOOKUP JOIN <index>`, `ENRICH`) read data that the namespace/type `filter` does not cover. The newer `TS` source command is also missing from the pattern. Fix: require the pipeline to start with `|` once trimmed. Better still, parse the full query and reject source commands, extra `FROM` targets and `LOOKUP JOIN`.

held.title: `esql` is imported from `@elastic/esql`, which may not be a dependency of this package.
held.body: The PR description says it uses `@kbn/esql-language`, but the import is `@elastic/esql`. If that package is not declared as a dependency of this core package (and in its tsconfig `kbn_references`), the build and runtime import will fail, and every `esql()` call breaks. I couldn't confirm the dependency setup from here. Fix: import from the declared Kibana package, or add the dependency explicitly.
